hints: Notice uranium-235 is given as proton number 92 and neutron number 143 - check which row keeps the proton number the same.
Recall isotopes have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, so $A = Z + N$ must change because $N$ changes.
Compare each row's proton number to 92 first, then check that its neutron number is not 143.
walkthrough: Identify the defining numbers for uranium-235: proton number $Z = 92$, neutron number $N = 143$, nucleon number $A = Z + N = 235$.
State the rule: isotopes of the same element have the same proton number $Z$ and different neutron number $N$, giving a different nucleon number $A$.
Check proton numbers in the table: only the row with $Z = 92$ can be uranium; rows with 91, 94 and 95 are different elements.
Check the $Z = 92$ row: it has $N = 144$ and $A = 236$, so $Z$ is unchanged while $N$ and $A$ differ from uranium-235.
This matches the definition of an isotope. This is option B.

options.A: Proton number 91 is different from 92, so it is a different element, not uranium, even though nucleon number is 235.
options.B: Proton number is 92, same as uranium-235, but neutron number 144 is different from 143, so it is an isotope of uranium.
options.C: Proton number 94 is different from 92, so it is a different element, even though neutron number 143 matches.
options.D: Proton number 95 is different from 92, so it is a different element, even though neutron number 143 matches.
